rule: A light source positioned at the top left or right gives more depth than one straight above the subject; light from below looks frightening.
In the front view the head is about five eye-widths wide and seven high, the eyes are halfway from crown to chin, and there is one eye-width between the eyes.
The line for the mouth is a little less than halfway between the line for the nose and the chin.
In the three-quarter view the nose bridge angles in toward the centre of the eyes and then angles out from the centre to the base of the nose.
In the side view the eye is drawn as a triangle placed about a third of the way from the front edge of the head circle.
A child's eyes are placed below the middle of the head, giving a bigger forehead, with a wide head and small features.
